title: Godot editor crashes Gnome session when dragging content from another program
body:
### Tested versions v4.5.stable.fedora [876b29033] ### System information Godot v4.5.stable (876b29033) - Fedora Linux 43 (Workstation Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) HD Graphics 530 (SKL GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700HQ CPU @ 2.60GHz (8 threads) - 15.42 GiB memory ### Issue description I tried to drag and drop a folder from my file explorer to the FileSystem dock in the Godot editor, and as soon as my cursor entered the window, my whole Gnome Session crashed, and I was brought back to the login screen. After some testing, I found that I can also reproduce the crash by selecting text in Firefox, and dragging it over to Godot's window.
Some logs that may be relevant (found them on the Problem Reporting app)

I also have a coredump.zst available, but I'm not sure if it contains sensitive data, so I won't upload it publicly here. But do tell me if it can be used to help diagnose the issue. ### Steps to reproduce There are might be some software config requirements to reproduce this crash, but I don't know what may be important or not, so here's what I'm running on: - Fedora 43 on Wayland with Gnome 49 (Linux 6.17.5-300.fc43.x86_64) - Intel HD Graphics 530 (SKL GT2) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 960M (with proprietary drivers v580.95.05) and some of my Godot Editor settings that may be relevant: - interface/multi_window/enable = true - run/platforms/linuxbsd/prefer_wayland = false I believe Godot is running under XWayland (I'm not sure how to check that). **Step to reproduce:** 1. Open Godot (no need to open a project, the crash happens even in the Project Manager) 2. Option A: open a file explorer (nautilus in my case) and start dragging any folder or file. (or) Option B: open firefox, highlight some text on any page and start dragging the selection. 3. Drag the element to the Godot window 4. Notice the entire Gnome session crash as soon as the cursor enters the window. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) NA
